sections.heading: Company profile
sections.body:
Global Hi-Tech Films is a manufacturer of paint protection films, automotive window films, and architectural window films with operations across more than 90 countries.

Industry: Manufacturing · Size: 1-49 · Products: Paint Protection Films, Automotive Window Films, Architectural Window Films, Sun Control Films, Safety & Security Films, Privacy Films

sections.heading: Qualification summary
sections.body: Global Hi-Tech Films scores 30 of 100 (tier disqualified) at 90% confidence. The score is carried by industry fit (12/30) and pain-point alignment (15/15). Nothing was found for application fit and event engagement, so those score zero rather than being estimated.

sections.heading: Tedlar angle
sections.body: They already market on uv resistance, chemical resistance, lifespan, which means the durability conversation is a product discussion rather than an education. Relevant Tedlar positioning: Tedlar PVF films hold colour and gloss through years of direct UV exposure. Tedlar resists solvents, cleaners and road chemicals without hazing. Tedlar overlaminates let printers underwrite longer graphic warranties.

sections.heading: Comparable accounts
sections.body: Closest known-good accounts: Avery Dennison Graphics Solutions (67% similar on films, protection, window, architectural); ORAFOL Europe (44% similar on films, graphic, performance, automotive); Mactac (43% similar on films, protection, specialty, graphic). Reference the comparable account by name on the call — a converter is far more persuaded by what a peer does than by a spec sheet.

sections.heading: Who to talk to
sections.body: No decision-maker resolved from public sources. Target titles for this ICP: VP Product, VP Product Development, VP Innovation, VP Research and Development, Director of R&D.

sections.heading: Gaps and risks
sections.body:
• Application fit: 4 more application area(s) would reach the ceiling.
• Event engagement: Confirming attendance at one more show would add points.
• Flags on the record: size third party estimate
